entry.focal: Split between the 2.4 m path_top_toro, which fills the left 22% of the frame from 1 m away, and the nearest white lantern post. The hero (brown 3 m box mid-frame) is visible but unlit, so it reads as a dark slab, not a toro.
entry.next_visible: Yes, but weakly: the cable-station box with two lit windows and the pool's lantern line sit low on the left horizon. No steam or teal glow reads.

reveal.focal: The hero box is centred and the largest thing in frame, but it is unlit; the two white posts on the right are brighter.
reveal.next_visible: The caldera water edge and its lanterns on the left, plus the cable station's dark box with a lit window. This is the best frame of the five spaces.

concept.focal: The near-left white lantern post plus the hero/stele pair, which read as two brown monoliths on the right. The intended match (Terrace Path lanterns dropping away down the west flank, cascade pools, cloud sea) is absent: the camera looks along a flat grey deck ending in sky.
concept.next_visible: No. The Terrace Path flights below are not visible from this camera; the deck just ends.

strip.focal: The hero box is a consistent landmark ahead in frames 0-4, which is good. Frames 1, 3 and 5 have a post or the hero box filling a third of the frame because the spine brushes them. Frames 6-7 are near-empty: a dark deck and the next space's lantern row.
strip.next_visible: The s_rim lantern row and cable station appear from frame 5 on; the hand-off is clear.

fixes.detail: The 1 m toro sits 1.27 m north of the spine centreline, so it intrudes about 0.4 m onto the 3.4 m deck and the walk brushes it (strip-4). Move it outward onto the rock lip. Make it emissive with a warm point light so it is the brightest object; right now every lantern_post outshines it.

The stele is 1.2 m off the spine, on the deck edge, and 2.8 m beyond the toro, so from the approach the toro hides it. Pull it back beside and slightly behind the toro (to about 65.2, 70.5) so the toro lights its face and both read as one stone group off the walk.

offset 0.8 -> 1.5 so the posts stand on the rail line rather than in the walking deck. Remove lights0:1 (59.6, 69.3) to leave a darker 8-10 m gap before the hero, so the toro is the light pool you walk into.

This rule produced 0 placements, so the north (crater) side of the walk is bare terrain. Fix the rule (probably avoid/embed rejecting everything) and bias the clusters to the stele/toro group and the two portals, not spread evenly.

It stands on the deck 1.2 m off the spine and 1 m from the entry camera, so it fills the entry frame. Move it to the rock edge. Also pull cameras.entry back to about (46.0, 75.6) so the toro frames the left edge instead of covering it.

top_change: Make the summit toro a lit, emissive point brighter than the posts and set it with the stele just off the deck, so the space has one warm focal stone instead of an unlit brown box beside a row of glowing pillars.
plausibility: Railings (dressing[0], snap 'structural') are not visible in any frame: there is no edge protection on the south-west drop. The rail pieces are 1.5 m long at about 4.7 m pitch, which leaves 3 m gaps even when rendered, and their z = floor + 1.0 suggests they may float 1 m up.

The deck reads as level ground at 120 m. From the walk there is no sense of a 120 m drop to the west/south-west and no view down the Terrace Path, so the 'top of 706 steps' moment is lost. The terrain beyond the rail needs to fall away within 2-3 m of the deck edge.
